subject.title: Bug: Built-in dreaming system contaminates agent identity in multi-agent setups

question: Should memory-core Dreaming enforce per-agent isolation by default for shared workspaces, or should workspace-level pooling remain an explicit operator-configured sharing mode?
rationale: Current docs promise isolated agent sessions, while the open fix candidate introduces config/API surface rather than a pure default isolation repair; maintainer intent is needed before accepting the durable boundary.

options.title: Require Default Agent Isolation
options.body: Treat cross-agent Dreaming corpus pooling as a security/session-state bug and require the fix to scope by current agent unless sharing is explicitly configured.

options.title: Accept Configured Allowlist
options.body: Accept the focused allowlist contract from the open PR as the first fix, but document that operators must configure it for shared-workspace isolation.

options.title: Define Workspace Pooling As Expected
options.body: Close or narrow this bug only if maintainers intentionally decide that shared workspace means shared Dreaming memory and update docs to make that explicit.

recommendation.title: Require Default Agent Isolation
recommendation.body: Treat cross-agent Dreaming corpus pooling as a security/session-state bug and require the fix to scope by current agent unless sharing is explicitly configured.

likelyOwner.reason: vincentkoc is assigned and already framed the exact shared-workspace isolation question in the issue discussion.
